title: Why the Dodge Viper Was Killed (Twice)
description:
The Dodge Viper was killed twice. The first time, in two thousand ten, American sales had fallen to three hundred ninety-two cars. The second time, in twenty seventeen, the maker said it was ending the car rather than redesign it for a new safety rule. In twenty twenty-six, the head of S R T explained that the rule would have put airbags right over the driver's ear. This is the story of why the Viper died, and why it died twice. Here is the twist. The popular explanation, that nobody wanted the car, is only part of the story. The sources point to a safety regulation that the Viper could not meet as built. And the second death came when the car was selling better than it had in years. We will show you the numbers, and tell you where sources disagree.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
